overrides.notes: Direct worked examples now include Gold and NQ, while Arjo separately identifies Metals, Indices and JPY pairs as easy-to-target classes; universal eligibility and exclusions remain unresolved.
Direct examples establish 4h/1h monitoring and a concrete NQ plan using 4h FVG, 1h FVA and 15m execution; no universal timeframe hierarchy is stated.
Arjo directly conditions LTF involvement on HTF expansion and provides an explicit 4h/1h/15m example, but the complete deterministic HTF-ready predicate remains unresolved.
The recovered long examples directly map a run of resistance/rejection high to one-sided bullish continuation toward ATH, but a complete direction algorithm across all PD Arrays remains unresolved.
Arjo requires competing/opposing arguments to be removed before involvement and gives a run of the 2CR high as a worked condition; the full argument inventory and weighting remain unresolved.
AoO is directly bounded from Trigger to Target and worked plans place LTF execution inside HTF expansion, but exact PD Array/FVA/FVG construction and setup selection remain incomplete.
A Run on Liquidity / Run of the 2CR high is directly identified as a trigger, with close-above and two-sting examples; alternative valid run constructions and tolerances remain unresolved.
Arjo states to enter when price trades into the AoO and gives a 15m execution example inside HTF/LTF context, but exact order type, fill price and confirmation timing remain unresolved.
Arjo gives a general invalid-probability boundary and an explicit bearish Swing-High stop example, but a directly stated deterministic long-side stop for this candidate is still missing.
Targets are directly constrained to PD Arrays and the recovered NQ plan targets the next ATH, but complete PD Array construction and tie-breaking among eligible targets remain unresolved.

Running a rejection high explicitly invalidates the prior respect interpretation and stop logic is tied to where the setup becomes low-probability, but post-entry invalidation remains under-specified.
Arjo says to move on when the required parameter is not met and requires trading within the WoO, but no universal bar-count or clock expiry rule is stated.
Trading is directly required to occur within a Window of Opportunity, implemented via a configured session or alerts; a universal fixed clock interval is intentionally not supplied.
A December-specific avoid-trading filter is directly documented, but it is calendar-specific and does not establish the complete optional-filter set for the candidate.

Direct evidence requires removing competing arguments before involvement and structures the trading plan as Bias, Narrative, Context, Entry and Risk Management; complete objective rules for every level remain unresolved.
